asof: Settles Fri 6 Nov 2026 · written Sat 7 Nov
headline: Payrolls beat retraces a third of Thursday's rally: H7–Z8 up 5–6bp, and the U7 peak at 4.39% prices just under two hikes.
summary: The strip sold off almost in parallel on Friday after a 165,000 payrolls print: Z7 and H8–M8 rose 6bp, H7, M7 and U7 5.5bp to 4.27%, 4.36% and 4.39%, and Z8 5bp to 4.35%, while Z6 lagged at +3.5bp to 4.145% and U6 barely moved at 3.92%. That reverses only about a third of Thursday's 14–16.5bp rally, so from the 30 October settle M7 and U7 are still 12–13bp lower, Z7 11bp, H7 8.5bp and the greens 6.5–7bp, with Z6 flat on the month. The peak stays in SR3U7 at 4.39%, 47bp over the 3.92% SOFR fixing, with 6bp of easing priced from there to Z9. Just under two hikes is a little more than the consensus of a December move plus one more in early 2027.
drivers: October payrolls rose 165,000 against 59,000–65,000 expected, September was revised up to 60,000 from 29,000, unemployment fell to 4.1% and hourly earnings rose 0.4% (3.1% on the year). The 2-year yield rose about 5bp to 4.52% and FedWatch odds for a December hike climbed back to roughly 76–85%. In SR3 the reds and greens led: H7 to Z8 rose 5–6bp in rate, Z6 3.5bp.
Tech rebound unwinds part of the haven bid

The Nasdaq rose about 1.5% and chip stocks about 4–6% after Thursday's AI-regulation rout, though the index stayed on course for a fourth weekly fall. Thursday's 16.5bp rally in M7 and U7 was only a third retraced, so most of the post-election repricing of 2027 hikes survives.
Fed speakers keep hikes on the table

San Francisco's Daly said more tightening is likely, at a deliberate, gradual pace, and New York's Williams called inflation too high for too long. With Hammack and Barkin also backing gradual hikes on Thursday, Reuters reported traders pulling the next-and-final hike forward to April from June; H7/M7 held at +9bp as both legs rose 5.5bp.
Oil and inflation expectations cap the selloff

Brent rebounded toward $100 on tanker attacks but was still heading for a weekly drop of 12–16%. Michigan sentiment rose to 51.0 against 48.0 expected, while one-year inflation expectations fell to 4.3% from 4.7% and the 5–10-year gauge to 3.4%, which kept the greens from following the reds fully: Z8–Z9 rose 4.5–5bp.
spreads: The whites steepened and the reds sold off in parallel. U6/Z6 widened 3.3bp to +22.5bp and Z6/H7 2bp to +12.5bp (−8.5bp on the month), while H7/M7 held at +9bp (−3.5bp) and M7/U7 at +3bp (−1bp); U7/Z7 rose 0.5bp to −0.5bp, so U7 stays the peak by half a basis point. Z6/Z7 widened 2.5bp to +24bp but is still 11bp tighter month-to-date, and Z6/M7 rose 2bp to +21.5bp (−12bp). Past the peak the inversion edged back: Z7/Z8 fell 1bp to −3.5bp (+4bp on the month), U7/Z8 0.5bp to −4bp (+6bp) and Z8/Z9 0.5bp to −2bp, with the green consecutive spreads between −1bp and 0. The H7/M7/U7 fly was unchanged at +6bp and M7/U7/Z7 slipped 0.5bp to +3.5bp (−2.5bp and −3bp on the month). Week- and month-to-date changes are the same, as both run from the 30 October settle.
fed: The latest fed funds futures snapshot is Thursday's, after the tech rout and before payrolls: 16.2bp for the 9 December meeting (a 65% chance of a hike), 21bp by January, 29.9bp by March, 39.9bp by June and a 44bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.32%). That is down from 20.4bp, 27bp, 41.4bp, 54.9bp and a 58bp peak on Wednesday, from 19.7bp, 28bp, 42.4bp, 59.1bp and 65bp a week earlier, and from the 30 October month-end (17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp, 57bp peak). Friday's SR3 settles already price the rebound: the 4.32% ZQ peak plus SOFR's 4bp premium over EFFR is 4.36%, 3bp under U7 at 4.39%, and Z6 at 4.145% is about 1.5bp over January ZQ plus that premium. After payrolls FedWatch put December back at roughly 76–85%. With Daly and Williams stressing too-high inflation, SR3's just-under-two-hike peak is a touch above the consensus of a December hike and one more in early 2027; Tuesday's CPI decides whether December is fully priced.

ideas.title: Stay short the H7/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and flat at +9bp: both legs rose 5.5bp in rate on payrolls, so the beat lifted the whole 2027 path rather than steepening it. Reuters reports traders pulling the last hike forward to April, which narrows the gap between the March and June periods; 6bp to target against 4bp to the stop keeps reward at 1.5 times risk.
ideas.risk: A hot October CPI on Tuesday could add hikes beyond April and push the spread through +13bp.

ideas.title: Keep 2028 easing as the hedge: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open, 4.5bp against entry at −3.5bp but 1bp in favour on Friday, as Z7 rose 6bp in rate and Z8 5bp. It did its job as a hedge to the core: a firmer data path sells the reds more than the greens. With 8.5bp to target and 4.5bp to the stop, reward is about 1.9 times risk.
ideas.risk: Another risk-off rally led by the reds would push the spread above +1bp and stop the hedge out.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 rose just 0.2bp to 3.92% implied on Friday, exactly the 3.92% SOFR fixing for 5 November, which is 2bp over the 3.90% interest on reserves, 4bp over the 3.88% EFFR and 8bp under the 4.00% standing repo rate. About $28bn of new refunding cash settles on 16 November and only U6's last week sees the December decision, so there is little to gain from an outright view.
ideas.risk: If funding stays soft, SOFR could slip toward 3.88–3.90% and leave a couple of bp on the table.

watch: $58bn, the first refunding sale, tests front-end demand after Friday's 5bp rise in 2-year yields.
The last CPI before the December meeting after 3.7% headline in September; it sets Z6, the December odds and the H7/M7 core.
$25bn after Wednesday's Veterans Day bond-market holiday; term premium and the greens.
Pipeline price pressure; a firm print would support 2027 hikes in the reds.
About $28bn of new cash settles; a funding test for SOFR and U6.
A renewed AI-stock selloff would revive the haven bid in the reds; tanker attacks that keep Brent near $100 would add to 2027 inflation risk.
